ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 6 — Preventive Visit — Gwen Ifill — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Ms. Ifill is a 60-year-old journalist with stage IIIC2 mismatch repair deficient endometrial cancer, treated with surgery and six cycles of dostarlimab, carboplatin and paclitaxel, who comes for her yearly preventive visit six weeks after the end of combination treatment. The CT then showed no evidence of disease. She had her first maintenance dose of dostarlimab six weeks ago and has her second today. Since starting levothyroxine her energy has improved and she no longer feels cold. The tingling in her toes is slowly fading. She has had no vaginal bleeding or discharge, pelvic pain, cough, leg swelling or weight loss. She is working full days again, covering the election campaign, and walks most mornings. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2016-08-11; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; weight 73.0 kg; blood pressure 124/78; pulse 70
Thyroid not enlarged or tender; no lymph nodes
Clinical breast examination with a chaperone, at her choice: no masses, skin or nipple changes, or axillary nodes
Port-site scars healed; soft, non-tender; no mass
No leg swelling; calf circumferences equal
Pinprick slightly reduced over the toes only; vibration and ankle reflexes normal; steady gait

Postmenopausal bleeding for three weeks, about eight years after her last period, in a woman of 60 who takes no hormone therapy: endometrial cancer must be excluded. Office endometrial biopsy taken today, transvaginal ultrasound this week, and gynecologic oncology review booked
S — Synthetic presenting problem; no symptom of her real illness was made public. Superseded by the diagnosis at the gynecologic oncology consultation.

Endometrioid adenocarcinoma of the endometrium, FIGO grade 2, mismatch repair deficient (loss of MLH1 and PMS2 staining), p53 wild-type pattern, on office endometrial biopsy, with enlarged right pelvic and para-aortic lymph nodes on CT; surgical staging planned; synthetic modern detail linked to her publicly reported endometrial cancer
S — Synthetic histology, molecular result and extent; her family gave endometrial cancer as the cause of death (D), and nothing more about it was made public.

Metastatic endometrioid carcinoma in the right external iliac sentinel lymph node (9 mm deposit) and a left para-aortic lymph node (14 mm deposit), with the other nodes removed negative: FIGO 2013 stage IIIC2ii
S — Synthetic nodal disease found at surgical staging.
Chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy from paclitaxel: tingling in the toes, grade 1 (sensory only, no effect on daily activities)
S — Synthetic common effect of paclitaxel.
Immune-related primary hypothyroidism from dostarlimab: TSH 11.8 with a low free T4, tiredness and feeling cold (grade 2)
S — Synthetic immune-related adverse event, among the most common with PD-1 inhibitors.

list.item:
Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated. Mammogram ordered: screening every two years from 40 to 74. Cervical screening is no longer indicated after total hysterectomy, and vaginal cytology is not used to look for recurrence. Colorectal screening is due: the cancer's mismatch repair loss was acquired, so average-risk screening applies, and she chose a stool immunochemical test. Lipids: total cholesterol 204, LDL 124, HDL 58 mg/dL; ten-year risk estimated as below the statin threshold, with lifestyle advice. A1c 5.5% earlier this year. [S]
Mammogram in two weeks.
Stool immunochemical test kit given today.
Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines this autumn.
Second zoster dose in two to six months.
Bone density at 65, sooner if a fracture or new risk factor.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Endometrioid endometrial cancer, FIGO stage IIIC2ii, MMRd, no evidence of disease (C54.1). No symptom or sign of recurrence. ALT 21 U/L and glucose 93 mg/dL before the second maintenance dose of dostarlimab, given today in the infusion center. [S]
Dostarlimab 1000 mg every six weeks.
Gynecologic oncology examination every three months; CT every six months for three years.

Immune-related hypothyroidism on dostarlimab (E03.2). TSH 3.6 and free T4 1.2 on levothyroxine 75 mcg; symptoms resolved. [S]
Continue levothyroxine 75 mcg daily.
TSH and free T4 every six weeks with the dostarlimab doses.

Follow-up: Mammogram in two weeks; stool test result by phone. Dostarlimab every six weeks with TSH, free T4, liver tests and glucose. Gynecologic oncology examination every three months and CT every six months. Influenza and COVID-19 vaccines this autumn. Next preventive visit in one year. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She wants full treatment aimed at cure and control of her cancer, wants to be told plainly what is happening, and wants to make her own decisions. She named a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here, and asked that information about her health be shared only with the people she names. She chose not to record other treatment preferences today. To be revisited yearly or if her illness changes. [S]
